A_nl_research.prompt: Research on-device AI agents using five credible academic or official sources. Compare their architecture, performance, privacy and limitations. Generate a professional PDF report and Excel comparison sheet with citations.
A_nl_research.message:
## Architecture
The evidence describes three distinct architectural approaches to on-device AI agents. Agent-X is presented as a software-only, accuracy-preserving framework that accelerates both the prefill and decode stages of on-device agent workloads, and is described as seamlessly integrable into existing on-device AI agents [1]. A second approach, Division-of-Thoughts (DoT), is a collaborative reasoning framework that leverages the synergy between locally deployed Smaller-scale Language Models (SLMs) and cloud-based LLMs, using an adapter for task allocation that is trained via a self-reinforced method relying solely on task execution feedback [2]. A third line of work centres on NNStreamer, a stream pipeline framework for on-device AI systems that handles neural networks with complex data stream pipelines on devices [3, 6]; the project aims to make each AI service atomic, re-deployable, and shared among connected devices of arbitrary vendors, and is a Linux Foundation (LF AI and Data) open source project accepting public contributions [3]. The brief does not provide further architectural detail (for example, model partitioning mechanics or memory layout) beyond these descriptions.
## Performance
Reported performance results are specific to each framework. Agent-X is reported to achieve a 1.61x end-to-end speedup on representative agentic workloads in real systems with no accuracy loss [1]. DoT is reported to significantly reduce LLM costs while maintaining competitive reasoning accuracy across extensive experiments on various benchmarks [2]. NNStreamer is described as significantly improving overall performance with minimal efforts [6], and its authors report that applying the stream pipeline framework saves developmental costs and hardware resources and improves performance [3], with the additional claim that it simplifies implementations and allows reusing off

> Evidence note: the collected sources did not cover limitations in the harvested evidence, so those sections report the gap instead of inventing detail.
